payload.text: Sneha sat in the art room one Tuesday and decided to paint a big picture. She painted a big yellow sun, a small bird and a tall green tree. She used three different brushes and was very careful with the edges so the colours did not run into each other. The teacher came over to her table and said it looked very pretty. Sneha was proud and decided to roll up the painting carefully and take it home to show her grandmother.

payload.title: Forgot Box EAR
payload.text: Aarav forgot his pencil box at home one morning and reached the art room with empty hands. The teacher said the lesson would need a pencil. Aarav felt worried for a moment. He then asked his friend Karan, who had brought two pencils that day. Karan shared one with Aarav with a big smile. Aarav promised he would bring an extra pencil for Karan next time so he could return the favour. The two friends finished the lesson together.

payload.title: Mother's Garden EAR
payload.text: Priya sat down at home one Saturday morning with her box of crayons and a clean sheet of paper. She drew a small garden filled with bright flowers and a big yellow sun above. She used five crayons of different colours, pressing carefully so the colours stayed bright. When she was done she ran to the kitchen to show her mother. Her mother smiled, kissed her forehead and stuck the drawing right on the fridge door for everyone to see.
payload.problem: Priya drew a garden for her mother

payload.title: Soggy Paper EAR
payload.text: Rohan was painting at home with water colours one afternoon. He forgot to dip his brush only lightly and used too much water on the page. The paper became soft and started tearing in the middle. Rohan felt upset and looked at the ruined picture. His sister came in and told him not to worry. She showed him how to use less water and pat the brush on the side of the cup. Rohan took a fresh sheet and started again, this time with better results.
payload.problem: Rohan used too much water and ruined his paper

payload.title: Wrong Fold EAR
payload.text: Diya was folding a paper boat in the art room with great care. She tried to follow the steps the teacher had shown but she made one wrong fold halfway through. The boat ended up looking like a crooked hat. She showed it to her brother who was sitting next to her. He laughed gently and said it was a common mistake. He showed her the right way to make the fold and the two of them made a proper paper boat together.
payload.problem: Diya made a wrong fold on her boat

payload.title: Sticky Mess EAR
payload.text: Kabir was making a paper craft in the art room when his elbow knocked over the open glue bottle. A sticky pool spread across the table top. Kabir's eyes widened and he stood up at once. He grabbed a stack of tissues and began cleaning the spill carefully. He then walked over to the teacher to say sorry. The teacher was happy that Kabir had cleaned up by himself without being told and gave him a small pat on the back.
payload.problem: Kabir spilled glue and cleaned it up

payload.title: Last Brush EAR
payload.text: Anaya had only one red brush left in the art room when Sneha walked over needing red paint too. Anaya thought about it for a moment, knowing she also needed the brush. Then she made up her mind. She washed her brush carefully under the tap and handed it to Sneha. She used a smaller spare brush from her own box for the rest of her painting. Sneha thanked her with a big smile and they both finished their paintings happily before the bell.

payload.title: Bright Rainbow EAR
payload.text: Aditya sat at home one rainy Sunday and decided to draw a bright rainbow with all seven colours in order. He worked carefully with his crayons, pressing each colour with care to keep the lines smooth. When he finished he felt very happy with how the rainbow had turned out. He found some tape in the drawer and stuck the picture right above his bed on the bedroom wall. Every morning after that he could see his rainbow first thing.

payload.title: Sunny Sky EAR
payload.text: Meera painted a yellow sun with three small clouds floating around it in the art room. She mixed her colours slowly so the sky did not turn muddy. The teacher walked over to her table and said her sky looked very real. Meera felt proud and decided to add more details. She painted a small bird flying across one corner of the sky. The teacher pinned her painting on the class board so all the kids could see it.
payload.problem: Meera painted a sunny sky with clouds

payload.title: Bubble Fish EAR
payload.text: Ishaan drew a blue fish inside a big water bowl in the art room. He added many small bubbles around the fish to make it look like it was really swimming. His friend leaned over and said the bubbles looked very cute. Ishaan thought about it for a moment and then added one more fish so the first one would not feel lonely in the bowl. The two fish looked like friends. The teacher smiled and said it was a thoughtful picture.
payload.problem: Ishaan drew two fish with bubbles

payload.title: Kite Tail EAR
payload.text: Arjun was making a paper kite at home for his cousin. The tail kept coming off because he was using only a tiny bit of tape. He tried again and again but the tape was just not strong enough. His sister came in to see what was wrong. She showed him how to use a longer piece of tape on both sides of the tail. Arjun fixed the tail carefully and at last the kite was ready to fly. He could not wait to give it to his cousin.
payload.problem: The kite tail kept falling off

payload.title: Star Sticker EAR
payload.text: Sara drew her house in the art room with her whole family standing outside the front door. She added her dog, a small tree and a sun in one corner of the page. She used different colours for each family member's clothes. The teacher came over, looked at the picture for a long time and gave her a shiny star sticker. Sara stuck the star right on top of the sun in her picture. She kept the drawing in her folder to take home.

payload.title: Mud Tree EAR
payload.text: Ravi sat down in the village ground one bright morning and started drawing a tall tree on the soft mud with a small stick. He drew the trunk first and then the branches one by one. His friends came over to see what he was doing. Soon they picked up their own sticks and started drawing their own trees right next to his. By the time they were done the whole patch was a tiny mud forest that they all admired together.
payload.problem: Ravi drew a tree and friends joined in

payload.title: Make Green EAR
payload.text: Tara walked through the art room and saw Sneha looking sad as she tried to mix yellow and blue paint to get green. The colour kept turning out wrong. Tara sat next to her and showed her how to mix slowly with small amounts of each colour. She told Sneha to dip the brush only a little at a time. Soon Sneha had a nice bright green colour ready in her dish. She thanked Tara warmly and finished her grass and trees with the new green.
payload.problem: Tara helped her friend mix green

payload.title: Lost Red EAR
payload.text: Karan was drawing a big red fire truck at home one afternoon. He reached into his pencil box for the red crayon but it was not there. He looked carefully under the table and behind his chair. He even checked his school bag. Finally he found the crayon tucked under the table near the leg where it had rolled. He picked it up with a big smile and finished his fire truck with bright red wheels and a tall ladder.
payload.problem: Karan searched for his lost red crayon

payload.title: Sparrow Picture
payload.text: Riya sat at home one quiet evening and drew a small bird sitting on a thin branch. She coloured the bird soft grey and made the branch brown. She added a few small leaves so the branch would not look empty. Her grandmother walked into the room and looked at the picture for a long moment. She said it looked just like a real sparrow she had seen in the garden the day before. Riya smiled and put the picture into her drawing folder for safekeeping.
payload.problem: Riya drew a sparrow on a branch

payload.title: Fast Car EAR
payload.text: Veer drew a fast red car with big black wheels in the art room. He gave the car a small driver inside wearing a yellow helmet. He even added a flag on the back of the car for fun. The teacher walked by, stopped to look and asked Veer if he would share his drawing with the whole class. Veer stood up shyly at first but then proudly showed the picture to everyone. The class clapped and one boy asked Veer if he would help him draw a car too.
payload.problem: Veer drew a fast car and shared it

payload.title: Pink Wings EAR
payload.text: Ananya painted a butterfly with pretty pink wings and tiny dots all over the wings in the art room. She added a small yellow flower beside the butterfly so it would have something to drink from. The teacher walked over and said the painting looked very lovely. She liked it so much that she pinned it right on the class board for all the kids to see. Ananya's friends came over to admire it. One of them asked Ananya to help her paint a butterfly too.
payload.problem: Ananya painted a butterfly with a flower

payload.title: Watering Girl EAR
payload.text: Anjali sat at home one Sunday and drew a small garden full of pink and yellow flowers. In the middle of the garden she drew a small girl holding a green water can and watering the plants. She added a butterfly above the flowers. Her mother came into the room, looked at the picture and laughed. She said the girl in the picture looked just like Anjali herself. Anjali smiled shyly and said it was meant to be her. They stuck the picture on the wall together.
payload.problem: Anjali drew herself in her garden picture

payload.title: Friendly Elephant EAR
payload.text: Vikram drew a big elephant with white tusks and grey skin in the art room. Next to the elephant he drew a small boy holding a small flower. His friend looked over from the next table and said the elephant looked very friendly. Vikram thought for a second and added a tiny smile on the elephant's face. Then he drew a small bird sitting on the elephant's back. The teacher walked by, smiled and asked him to share the picture with the class.
payload.problem: Vikram drew a friendly elephant and boy

payload.title: Group Song EMU2
payload.text: Sneha sang a school song with her whole class in the music class one bright Monday morning. They all kept the same beat and ended together perfectly. The teacher smiled and said the group had sounded really nice. Sneha was very happy that she had been part of a group that worked together so well. After class she walked out humming the tune. She told her friends that singing together felt better than singing alone.
payload.problem: Sneha sang in a tight group song

payload.title: New Tune EMU
payload.text: Aarav learned a new tune on the keyboard at home over the long weekend. He played it slowly first to get all the notes right and his fingers in the correct positions. Then he tried it a little faster, then faster still until it sounded smooth. His father came into the room one evening, listened to him play and said it sounded very nice. Aarav felt proud and decided to learn one more new tune by next weekend if he could.
payload.problem: Aarav learned a new keyboard tune

payload.title: Stuck Key EMU
payload.text: Priya was playing the harmonium in the music class when one key suddenly got stuck and would not come back up. She stopped playing and felt worried because the song could not continue. She told the teacher about it right away without panicking. The teacher carefully lifted the key with her fingers and fixed it gently. Priya thanked the teacher and then played the whole song from the start without a single problem. The class clapped for her at the end.

payload.title: Mic Line EMU
payload.text: Rohan stood on the stage during morning assembly and sang one line of the national song into the mic. He had practised it many times at home. The whole school listened in silence and his voice came out clear. After the song ended his class clapped for a long time. The principal walked over and patted him on the shoulder. Rohan smiled and walked back to his row feeling very proud. His best friend gave him a thumbs up from the line.
payload.problem: Rohan sang on the assembly mic

payload.title: First Clear Note
payload.text: Diya had been trying to blow a clear note on her flute at home for many days. Every time the note came out airy or weak. On a quiet Sunday morning she tried again with a small breath. This time the note rang out softly and clearly across the room. She felt very excited and ran straight to her grandmother. She played the note again for her. Her grandmother clapped loudly and asked her to play one more time. Diya beamed with pride.
payload.problem: Diya finally played a clear flute note

payload.title: Drum Beat EMU
payload.text: Kabir was on the drum in the music class while his friends sang the school song. He kept a steady beat right through the song without a single mistake even when the song speed changed slightly. The teacher smiled and said his beat had been perfect from start to end. Kabir felt very proud and a little tired from focusing so hard. His friends came over after class and asked him to teach them how to keep a steady beat too.
payload.problem: Kabir kept a steady drum beat

payload.title: Picked Duo
payload.text: Anaya and Riya sang together in the music class as a pair for the first time. Their voices matched well and blended into one soft sound. The teacher liked it so much that she picked both of them to sing for the school day next month. The two girls hugged each other and ran out to tell their parents. Their parents promised to come and watch them perform. Anaya and Riya planned to practise together every day after school until the big day.
payload.problem: Anaya was picked to sing for school day

payload.title: Wrong Note Fix EMU
payload.text: Aditya sang a wrong note in the music class one afternoon and felt very shy. His face turned red and he stopped singing. His friends did not laugh at him. Instead one of them hummed the correct note softly so Aditya could match it. He listened carefully, found the right note and joined back into the song. After class Aditya thanked his friend for helping him without making a fuss. He said it had made the whole thing feel okay.

payload.title: Folk Evening
payload.text: Meera sang an old village folk song in the village ground with her cousin one warm evening. The tune was one she had learned from her grandmother. Her grandmother heard the song from the porch and came out to join them. The three of them sang together until the sun went down behind the trees. The neighbours clapped softly from their windows. Meera felt very happy and proud that she could pass on the song to her cousin too.
payload.problem: Meera sang a folk song with family

payload.title: Broken String EMU
payload.text: Ishaan was playing his toy guitar at home when one of the strings suddenly snapped with a small ping. He felt sad and looked at the broken end. He went to his older brother for help. His brother smiled, found a new string in his drawer and tied it carefully to the right place on the guitar. He helped Ishaan tune it just right. Soon the guitar was ready again and they made small tunes together for the rest of the afternoon.
payload.problem: A string broke on Ishaan's guitar

payload.title: Soft Humming EMU
payload.text: Arjun was sitting at his desk at home and drawing pictures one quiet afternoon. He started humming a school song softly as he worked. His little sister came into the room and listened for a moment. She said she really liked the tune and asked him what song it was. Arjun smiled and sang it a little louder for her. She picked it up quickly and they ended up humming the song together until their mother called them for snack time.
payload.problem: Arjun hummed a song with his sister

payload.title: Clap Race
payload.text: Sara clapped to the beat with her friends in the music class as a warm-up. The teacher then turned it into a small game by making the beat faster and faster each round. Some kids dropped out as the speed increased. Sara stayed with the beat the longest by focusing only on the teacher's hands. She won the round and her friends clapped for her at the end. The teacher gave her a small star sticker. Sara stuck it on her notebook.

payload.title: Grandfather Beat EMU
payload.text: Ravi sat in the village ground one evening with his grandfather and tapped on a small village drum. His grandfather showed him a simple beat and clapped along to keep time. Ravi listened carefully and learned the beat quickly. He joined in and the two played together for a while. Soon the other children in the village heard the sound and gathered around to listen. Some of them clapped along too. Ravi felt proud that he was making music with his grandfather.
payload.problem: Ravi learned a beat from his grandfather

payload.title: Big Stage EMU
payload.text: Tara sang on the big school stage during the annual function in front of all the parents and teachers. Her hands were shaking a little at the start but her voice was steady all the way through the song. The audience listened in silence and clapped for a long time when she finished. Her teacher hugged her backstage and said it was one of the best songs of the evening. Tara's parents took her out for ice cream after the show to celebrate.
payload.problem: Tara sang well on the big stage

payload.title: Forgot Words EMU
payload.text: Karan was singing his song on the school stage during the annual function. Halfway through, his mind suddenly went blank and the words slipped away. He stopped and looked nervous in front of the audience. His friend from the side of the stage whispered the next line for him just loud enough to hear. Karan smiled with relief, picked up the words and finished the song confidently. The audience clapped warmly. After the show he gave his friend a big thank you and a high five.
payload.problem: Karan forgot the song words on stage

payload.title: Sweet Voice EMU
payload.text: Riya sang a sweet song in the music class with a soft and calm voice one afternoon. The teacher said her singing sounded like a small stream flowing gently through the room. The other kids clapped quietly when she finished so they would not break the calm. Riya felt very happy and a little shy. After class her friend told her that her voice was the most peaceful in the whole class. Riya thanked her friend with a soft smile and a hug.
payload.problem: Riya sang in a soft sweet voice

payload.title: Home Parade EMU
payload.text: Veer blew a toy trumpet at home one sunny afternoon and his sister giggled every single time. He tried to make a simple tune by changing his breath and lip pressure. They started a small parade around the room together with his sister leading the way. Their mother came in to see what the noise was about and joined them by clapping along to the beat. The three of them marched around the room three times before sitting down for water and a small snack.
payload.problem: Veer led a small home parade

payload.title: Steady Through EMU
payload.text: Ananya kept the same steady beat through the whole song in the music class on a Wednesday afternoon. She did not lose it even once even when the other voices changed speed. The teacher stopped the class at the end and told everyone that keeping the beat is the most important skill in music. Ananya felt proud and gave the class a small smile. After class her friends asked her how she did it. She said she just focused on the teacher's hand.

payload.title: Quiet Help EMU
payload.text: Anjali noticed that Sneha was singing the wrong note in the music class one afternoon. She did not want to embarrass her friend in front of the others. Without making a fuss she quietly hummed the correct note close to Sneha's ear. Sneha caught the right note quickly and the song sounded balanced again. The teacher had been watching and smiled because she had seen everything. After class she told Anjali that helping a friend so kindly was a wonderful thing to do.
payload.problem: Anjali helped a friend get the note right

payload.title: Soft Please EMU
payload.text: Vikram was singing so loudly in the music class that the other voices got completely drowned out. The teacher gently called him aside and asked him to sing softer so everyone could be heard. Vikram nodded, lowered his voice and started listening more carefully to the rest of the group. The song then sounded balanced and the class clapped at the end. The teacher told him that singing in a group means listening as much as singing. Vikram thought about it and agreed.

payload.title: Society Six ESP
payload.text: Aarav was batting in the society lane match on a Sunday afternoon with his friends watching from the side. The fast bowler ran in and bowled a slightly short delivery. Aarav swung hard and hit a big six right over the watchman's small room near the gate. His teammates ran out cheering to find the ball and bring it back. The watchman came out smiling and rolled the ball back to the lane. Aarav waved to him in thanks.
payload.problem: Aarav hit a big six over the watchman's room

payload.title: First Goal ESP
payload.text: Priya was playing football at the school sports field during a friendly match between two classes. The ball came to her near the goal. She controlled it with her left foot, took a small breath and kicked it past the keeper into the net. It was her very first goal in any match. Her team lifted her up and cheered for a long time. Her coach gave her a small high five and said she had played with real courage and skill.

payload.title: Long Rally ESP
payload.text: Rohan and his sister played a very long badminton rally at home one rainy afternoon. The shuttle went back and forth more than twenty times without touching the floor. Both of them moved quickly across the small space. Finally Rohan missed a soft drop near the wall and the rally ended. They both laughed and started counting hits again for the next round. They played until evening when their mother called them for tea and snacks. Rohan said it was one of his best games.
payload.problem: Rohan played a very long rally

payload.title: Kabaddi Catch ESP
payload.text: Diya was defending in a kabaddi match at the sports field during sports day. The raider from the other team came in confidently and tried to touch many players. Diya stayed calm in her corner and watched carefully for her chance. When the raider got close she lunged forward and caught him by the leg. Her team won the point and went on to win the whole match. Diya's coach gave her a small medal at the end of the day for her brave defending.
payload.problem: Diya caught the raider and won the match

payload.title: Race Win ESP
payload.text: Kabir lined up for the short race on sports day at the school field one bright morning. He focused only on the finish line and forgot about the other runners. When the whistle blew he ran with all his strength. He came first by a few steps and broke the small ribbon at the finish line. The teacher pinned a small medal on his shirt and his class clapped loudly. His parents had come to watch and his father lifted him up in a hug.
payload.problem: Kabir came first in the race

payload.title: Relay Trophy ESP
payload.text: Anaya was the last runner in the relay race at the school sports field. She waited at the line as her teammates ran their parts of the race. When her friend handed her the baton she took off with all her speed. She ran fast and crossed the finish line first. Her team got a small trophy at the end of the day. She showed it proudly to her mother that evening at home. Her mother kept the trophy on the living room shelf.
payload.problem: Anaya helped her team win the relay

payload.title: One Run Loss ESP
payload.text: Aditya's cricket team needed just two runs to win at the school field. He played a careful shot to gully and got only one run before the last ball. The next batter then got out on the final delivery. His team lost the match by one run. Aditya felt very sad and sat on the boundary for a long time. His coach walked over and told him he had played well and should try again next time. Aditya wiped his eyes and nodded.
payload.problem: Aditya's team lost by one run

payload.title: Twisted Foot ESP
payload.text: Meera was running fast in a match at the sports field when she twisted her foot on a small stone hidden in the grass. She sat down right where she was, holding her ankle and trying not to cry. Her friend saw her from across the field and ran over to call the teacher. The teacher arrived quickly with an ice pack and gently put it on Meera's foot. After a short rest Meera felt a little better and was able to limp to a bench.

payload.title: Help Teammate ESP
payload.text: Ishaan was chasing the football at the sports field during a school match. He saw his teammate trip and fall down hard near the goal. The match was still going on but Ishaan stopped chasing the ball. He ran over and helped his friend stand up first. The coach watched it from the sideline. After the match he told Ishaan that good play also means caring for teammates first. Ishaan smiled and said he would always help a friend before chasing the ball.
payload.problem: Ishaan stopped to help a fallen teammate

payload.title: Caught Out ESP
payload.text: Arjun was playing cricket in the village field one bright morning with a wooden bat his grandfather had made for him. He took his stance carefully when the bowler ran in. He hit a straight shot back at the bowler with too much force. The bowler stuck out a hand and caught it cleanly. Arjun was out and felt a little upset. He laughed it off, handed the bat to the next batter and went to sit with his teammates. They told him it had been a good shot anyway.
payload.problem: Arjun got caught out by the bowler

payload.title: Long Hit ESP
payload.text: Ravi was batting in the village field on a bright morning with his friends watching. He hit a long shot deep into the open field for runs. He ran back and forth four times while his team cheered loudly from the side of the field. The other team finally got the ball back and threw it to the bowler. By that time Ravi had got four big runs from a single shot. He raised the bat to thank his teammates for cheering him on.
payload.problem: Ravi ran four runs after a long hit

payload.title: Keeper Save ESP
payload.text: Sara was the goalkeeper at the school sports field in a tough match against the other section. The other team got a free kick close to the goal. The striker took a hard kick aimed at the top corner. Sara dived to her left and just managed to push the ball away with her fingertips. Her team cheered loudly and patted her on the back at the next break. Her coach said it was one of the best saves he had seen all season.

payload.title: Last but Brave ESP
payload.text: Tara ran the race at the school sports field on sports day but came last. She felt very sad and tears began to well up in her eyes. Her friend walked up to her and told her that trying hard was the most important thing of all. Tara took a deep breath and gave a small smile. She said she would practise more often before the next sports day. Her friend gave her a hug and they walked over to the water station together for a drink.
payload.problem: Tara came last but kept her spirit

payload.title: Clean Bowled ESP
payload.text: Karan was batting in the society lane match on a Sunday morning with his friends watching from the steps. The bowler ran in and bowled a fast straight ball that beat his bat completely and hit the stumps. Karan was clean bowled and felt embarrassed for a moment. He walked back to the side slowly with the bat in his hand. He waved to the next batter and cheered him on from the side. Later he asked the bowler how he had spun the ball so fast.

payload.title: Net Drop ESP
payload.text: Riya was playing badminton at the sports field with her doubles partner during practice. She tried a hard smash but hit the shuttle straight into the net instead. They lost the point and Riya felt a little annoyed at her own shot. She thought for a moment and decided to change her approach. Next time the shuttle came to her she tried a slow lift to the back of the court. The other pair was caught off guard and Riya's team won the rally.
payload.problem: Riya hit the shuttle into the net

payload.title: Match Save ESP
payload.text: Veer was the goalkeeper at the sports field during the school football final. The match was very tight and the score was tied with just one minute left on the clock. The other team got a corner kick and took a hard shot at the goal. Veer jumped up and pushed the ball over the bar with his fingertips. The whistle blew and his team won the match on penalties later. His teammates ran over and lifted him up in the air with joy.

payload.title: Photo Cup ESP
payload.text: Ananya's team won the small cup at the school sports day after a close and exciting final match. She was asked to hold the cup high for the team photo. The team gathered around her and grinned at the camera. Her parents clapped from the side and were very proud of her. After the photo she held the cup all the way home to show her grandmother. Her grandmother kept it in the front room so every visitor could see it.

payload.title: Long Race ESP
payload.text: Sneha lined up for the long race at the school sports field one Saturday morning. She was tired by the second round and her legs felt heavy as logs. She wanted to stop but she had promised herself she would finish. She kept going one step at a time. When she finally crossed the line her coach gave her a big smile and a cold bottle of water. He said finishing what you start is more important than winning. Sneha smiled and nodded as she caught her breath.
payload.problem: Sneha finished a tiring long race

payload.title: Water Share ESP
payload.text: Anjali noticed that her teammate looked very tired during the break at the sports field. She had her own water bottle and only one was left. She walked over and offered the bottle to her teammate. Her teammate took a long drink, gave a tired smile and said thank you. After the break both of them played even better in the second half of the match. The coach said good teammates lift each other up. Anjali felt proud of her small kind act and shared a snack too.
payload.problem: Anjali shared water with a tired teammate

payload.title: Lost Ball ESP
payload.text: Vikram was batting in the society lane match on a Sunday afternoon and the bowler was running in. He swung hard at a half volley and hit the ball so cleanly that it flew over the boundary wall and disappeared from sight. The match had to pause for many minutes while everyone tried to figure out where the ball had gone. Vikram and his friends searched in the lane next door for a long time. Eventually they found another ball at a friend's house and the match started again.
payload.problem: Vikram hit the ball over the wall and lost it

payload.title: Clever Fox ELB
payload.text: Aarav read a short story about a clever fox in the school library after class one Tuesday afternoon. The fox in the story tricked a crow into dropping a piece of cheese on the ground. Aarav liked the trick part of the story the most and could picture every scene in his head. He went over to the librarian and told her he wanted to read the next story by the same writer. The librarian smiled and said the next book was already on the shelf for him.

payload.title: Quiet Please ELB
payload.text: Priya was reading a new story in the school library when her friend walked in and started talking loudly. She did not want him to get in trouble with the librarian. She put a finger to her lips and gently asked him to lower his voice. Her friend said sorry and started whispering instead. The librarian smiled at Priya from her desk and gave her a small thumbs up. Priya went back to her book feeling glad that the quiet rule of the library was kept.
payload.problem: Priya asked her friend to be quiet

payload.title: Brave Boy ELB
payload.text: Rohan picked a new comic book about a brave boy who saved a small village in the school library. He sat in a corner near the window and got lost in the story right away. He finished the book in one sitting without even noticing the time. When he returned it to the librarian he asked if there was a next part. The librarian said the next part would arrive soon and promised to keep one copy for him.
payload.problem: Rohan finished a comic in one sitting

payload.title: Late Return ELB
payload.text: Diya returned a story book a day late to the school librarian on a Monday morning. She felt sorry and said it had been raining heavily on Sunday so she could not come to school. The librarian listened kindly and said it was fine this time. She reminded Diya that returning books on time helps other kids who are waiting to read them too. Diya nodded and promised to plan ahead better. She picked a new book for the week and walked out feeling determined to be on time.
payload.problem: Diya returned a book a day late

payload.title: Honest Tear ELB
payload.text: Kabir was turning a page in the school library when the corner suddenly tore by mistake. He felt sad for a moment and looked at the small tear. He could have just put the book back without saying anything. Instead he walked straight to the librarian and showed her what had happened. The librarian thanked him for telling the truth and got out her tape. Together they taped the page back together neatly. Kabir went back to his table feeling glad that he had been honest.
payload.problem: Kabir tore a page and owned up to it

payload.title: Animal Shelf ELB
payload.text: Anaya was reading a story at her usual table in the school library when a small kid from the lower class walked up and asked her for help. He wanted to find a book about lions. Anaya put a bookmark in her own book and took him to the animal section. She pointed out a few good books on the lower shelf that had pictures of lions. The small kid picked one with bright pictures and said a big thank you to Anaya.
payload.problem: Anaya helped a small kid find a lion book

payload.title: Train Pictures ELB
payload.text: Aditya read a picture book about colourful trains in the school library after lunch one afternoon. He looked at every picture twice and read the small captions very carefully. He liked the bright steam engines the most. After he finished the book he turned to his friend and said he wanted to become a train driver one day. His friend laughed and said he wanted to become a pilot instead. The two friends sat together for a while and made plans for their future jobs in great detail.
payload.problem: Aditya read a picture book about trains

payload.title: Top Shelf ELB
payload.text: Meera wanted a book that was on the very top shelf in the school library but she could not reach it on her own. She stretched up on her toes but the shelf was still too high. She thought for a moment and then walked over to the librarian to ask for help politely. The librarian smiled, brought a small wooden stool and took the book down for her. Meera thanked her and took the book to her favourite table near the window. She read it happily.
payload.problem: Meera could not reach the top shelf

payload.title: Bag Find ELB
payload.text: Ishaan was sure he had lost his library book and started looking everywhere in the school library. He checked under chairs and behind the shelves. The librarian saw him searching and gently suggested he check his school bag carefully first. Ishaan opened his bag and dug through his things. He found the book at the very bottom of his bag under his lunch box. He laughed at himself and went over to say sorry to the librarian for the worry. She just smiled and said it happens to everyone.
payload.problem: Ishaan thought he had lost his book

payload.title: Van Story ELB
payload.text: Arjun climbed into the village library van when it stopped near his house one Saturday morning. He picked a story book about a clever boy and a king from the small shelf inside. He sat on the bench inside the van and read happily for nearly an hour. The librarian on the van said he could borrow the book to finish it at home. Arjun thanked her and walked back to his house with the book held carefully in both hands. He read it under the neem tree until evening.
payload.problem: Arjun read a king story in the van

payload.title: Pretty Princess ELB
payload.text: Sara walked through the school library and saw a book with a pretty blue cover on a low shelf. The cover had a small girl holding a kite. She picked it up and started reading from the first page right there. The story was about a princess who built her own kite to fly to the clouds. Sara loved the story so much that she borrowed the book to finish it at home that evening.
payload.problem: Sara picked a princess kite story

payload.title: Van Borrow ELB
payload.text: Ravi waited near the village square for the library van to arrive on Thursday afternoon. He had been thinking about new books all week. When the van finally came he climbed in and chose a small story book about a farmer's clever son. He thanked the librarian and walked home holding the book carefully. He sat under the neem tree in his yard and read the whole story until the sun set. He could not wait to share the story with his younger sister at dinner.
payload.problem: Ravi borrowed a farmer story from the van

payload.title: Read Aloud ELB
payload.text: Tara was sitting in the school library next to her friend who loved listening to stories. The two of them shared one book between them. Tara read aloud softly so they did not disturb the other kids around them. Her friend turned the pages at the right moments. They were so quiet that the librarian came over only to smile and give them a soft thumbs up. The two friends finished the story together and decided to share another book the next day too.
payload.problem: Tara read aloud softly to a friend

payload.title: Five Books ELB
payload.text: Karan picked five different books from the shelves in the school library one afternoon. He carried them carefully in his arms to a table near the window where he liked to sit. He sat down and read a little of each book to decide which one to take home for the week. Some were too easy and some were too hard for him. In the end he picked two books that were just right and put the other three back on the right shelves.
payload.problem: Karan picked five books to look at

payload.title: Word List
payload.text: Riya was reading a story in the school library but many words in it were new to her. She read slowly and tried to guess the meanings from the sentences around them. She took out her small notebook and wrote down three of the new words to ask her teacher the next day. The librarian came over and said writing down new words is a very smart way to read. Riya smiled and felt proud.
payload.problem: Riya was learning new words from a story

payload.title: Long Hunt ELB
payload.text: Veer searched the shelves of the school library for his favourite book about space. He looked in the usual row near the science section but it was not there. He looked in two more rows and was about to give up. Just then he spotted it tucked into the wrong row by mistake. He pulled it out happily and took it back to his table. Later he showed it to the librarian and asked her to put it in the right place so others could find it easily.
payload.problem: Veer found his book in the wrong row

payload.title: Sister's Book ELB
payload.text: Ananya picked a new story book about a small puppy in the school library after class. The story made her laugh many times as she sat at the table. She decided to borrow it so she could read it aloud to her younger sister at home. That evening she sat with her sister on the bed and read the whole story slowly. Her sister loved the puppy in the story so much that she asked Ananya to read it again the next night. Ananya was happy to share the book.

payload.title: Soft Whisper ELB

payload.text: A new girl stood quietly at the edge of the playground, watching the others run around in a game of tag. payload.problem: Kabir wanted to make friends with the new neighbour

payload.text: Diya's cousin came all the way from the village to spend the long summer holidays at her home. payload.title: A Kind Welcome
payload.text: On his very first day at the new school, a boy did not know where to keep his bag or which classroom was his own. payload.title: You Bat Next
payload.text: A new boy stood at the side of the field, watching the cricket match with longing in his eyes. payload.title: Take My Colours

payload.title: A Sweet Start
payload.text: It was the new kid's very first day at school, and he sat all alone at the back of the big school hall. payload.title: Share My Desk
payload.text: When a new boy came to the class, the teacher kindly told him to go and find an empty seat. The boy stood awkwardly near the door, holding his bag and not knowing what to do, while the whole class watched him. His face slowly turned red with worry. Arjun quickly slid all his own books to one side and made enough space at his own desk for the new boy.
payload.problem: Arjun wanted to make room for the new boy

payload.title: Play Football
payload.text: After school each day, the children gathered at the playground for their favourite game of football. One afternoon a new boy stood near the goalpost all by himself, watching the others pick their teams. Nobody called his name or asked him to join, and he slowly began to turn away to go home alone. He had hoped so much to make a friend that day. Rohan saw the boy walking off sadly, jogged over, passed him the ball with a smile, and asked him to come and join the match.
payload.problem: Rohan wanted a new friend to play football with

payload.title: New Girl in Society
payload.text: Tara met a new girl who had just shifted into her building with her whole family. The girl did not know where the children played in the evenings or which swing in the park was the best one. She wandered near the society gate, looking unsure and a little lost, not daring to ask anyone for help. She had nobody to show her around the new place. Tara felt for her, so she took the girl on a friendly tour of the whole society and showed her all the nicest spots in the park.
payload.problem: Tara wanted to help the new girl settle into the society

payload.title: Here, Borrow This
payload.text: The class test had just begun, and everyone was busy writing, when the new boy realised he had no pencil at all. He searched his bag in a rising panic, turning out every pocket, but there was nothing he could write with. He could not even begin his paper, and the big clock on the wall was ticking away the minutes. He looked around helplessly, too shy to ask the teacher. Ishaan noticed the new boy's worried face, quietly leaned across, handed him a spare pencil, and whispered to him not to worry at all.
payload.problem: Ishaan wanted to help the new boy during the test

payload.title: Friends at the Party
payload.text: At a cousin's lively birthday party held at home, Riya noticed a girl she had never seen before. The girl stood quietly near the cake table, not playing with anyone, and looking very left out from all the fun. Everyone else had already paired up into happy little groups, laughing and dancing together. The new girl looked like she wanted to slip away and go home. Riya did not want her to feel alone, so she went straight over, said a cheerful hi, and the two of them played party games together all evening.
payload.problem: Riya wanted to make a new friend at the party

payload.title: Come on the Slide
payload.text: At the park one breezy evening, Ananya spotted a new boy sitting all by himself on a wooden bench. He kept looking up at the tall, shiny slide, but he never once went up to try it, as if he were scared or simply too shy. The other children climbed and slid happily, paying him no attention at all. The boy looked lonelier with every passing minute. Ananya could not bear to see him alone, so she called out cheerfully, ran up the slide steps, and asked him to come and slide down with her.
payload.problem: Ananya wanted to make the lonely boy a playmate

payload.title: Sit Beside Me
payload.text: On the crowded school van one busy morning, a new boy climbed in and did not know where he was supposed to sit. He stood in the narrow aisle, holding tightly to a seat, looking unsure and uneasy as the van started to move along the bumpy road. A few children stared at him, and some even giggled, which made him feel worse. He wished he could just disappear from sight. Karan noticed his distress, patted the empty seat right beside him with a smile, and chatted happily with the boy all the way to school.
payload.problem: Karan wanted to make the new boy feel comfortable

payload.title: A Cheerful Hi
payload.text: During the long break, Vikram noticed a new kid standing all alone in the busy corridor. The kid clutched his books tightly to his chest and seemed far too shy to talk to any of the children rushing past him. He looked as if he wished he could simply melt into the wall and not be seen by anyone. Nobody stopped to say a single word to him. Vikram felt for the lonely kid, so he walked right over with a big, friendly grin, said a cheerful hi, and asked the new kid what his name was.
payload.problem: Vikram wanted to be friendly to the shy new kid

payload.title: Find Your Seat
payload.text: A new classmate walked into the room a little late and could not find a place to sit anywhere. She stood nervously near the door, glancing around the crowded class helplessly, while the teacher had not yet arrived to help her. Every face turned to look at her, and her cheeks slowly turned bright red with worry and shyness. She did not know a single person there. Anjali saw how uncomfortable the new girl was, so she quickly waved her over, pointed to the empty seat beside her, and kindly gave her a spare book to use.
payload.problem: Anjali wanted to help the new girl find a seat

payload.title: Quick Friends
payload.text: On the very first morning of the new term, Sneha found herself sitting next to a new girl who seemed quite nervous and unsure. The girl kept her bag tightly on her lap and barely spoke a single word, looking around the strange classroom with wide, worried eyes. Sneha could tell that she was scared of not making any friends in the new school. She decided that she would be the one to break the ice. They began to talk about their favourite books and games, and by the end of the day they had become the closest of friends.
payload.problem: Sneha wanted to make friends with the nervous new girl

payload.title: Missing Pencil
payload.text: Ravi opened his pencil box to begin his classwork, but his brand-new pencil was simply not there. He searched carefully under his desk, inside every single pocket of his bag, and even on the dusty floor nearby. His kind friends saw him looking worried and got down to help him search all around the desks too. They lifted books and peeked into corners, but it was no use. No matter how hard everyone looked, the new pencil had completely vanished from the class.
payload.problem: Ravi could not find his missing pencil
problemDecoys: Ravi had made a new friend

payload.title: The Lunchbox Hunt
payload.text: When the lunch bell rang out loudly, Priya happily reached into her school bag for her food. To her great shock, her shiny steel lunchbox was not inside the bag at all. She checked every zip and pocket twice, then asked all her friends if they had seen it anywhere. She even bent down to look under all the wooden benches in the room. But it was all in vain, for the lunchbox was simply nowhere to be found in the whole school.

payload.title: Only One Slipper
payload.text: Aarav had been running, jumping, and chasing his friends around the park all through the evening. When the sky finally turned dark and his mother called him home, he went to put his slippers back on. To his dismay, he found only one slipper lying near the wooden bench. The other one had slipped off somewhere while he was playing, and he had not noticed at all. He searched behind every bush and under the slide, but the missing slipper was lost.
payload.problem: Aarav lost one of his slippers

payload.title: The Runaway Coin
payload.text: Anaya held a shiny new one-rupee coin tightly in her small fist as she walked home from the shop. Near the society gate, she stopped for a moment to watch a pretty butterfly flutter past her. In that little moment, the coin slipped right out from between her fingers. It hit the ground, rolled away very fast, and dropped straight into a narrow crack in the pavement. Anaya knelt down and searched and searched with her tiny fingers, but the coin was well and truly lost.

payload.title: Cap Left Behind
payload.text: Kabir was talking and laughing happily with his best friend as the school van reached his stop. In his great hurry to climb down and get home, he completely forgot about his favourite blue cap lying on the seat. The van door shut and it drove off down the road before he could remember to grab it. He walked home cheerfully, not knowing what he had left behind. Only when he reached his door and looked for his cap did he realise, with a sinking feeling, that it was gone.

payload.title: The Dog Ran Out
payload.text: One sleepy afternoon, the society gate was accidentally left wide open when a delivery man walked through it. Before anyone could rush to shut it again, Diya's little pet dog spotted his chance and dashed straight outside onto the busy road. Diya saw him bolt and ran after him as fast as she could, calling his name over and over. But the dog was quick and excited, and he darted around a corner. By the time Diya reached the street, her dog was nowhere to be seen anywhere.

payload.title: Lost on the Way
payload.text: Aditya's mother gave him a very important letter and asked him to post it at the post office. He held it carefully in his hand and set off down the long lane towards the office. On the way, he stopped for a while to watch a colourful kite dancing high up in the bright sky. He was so caught up in the lovely sight that he forgot all about the letter. When he finally reached the post office, his hands were empty; the letter had slipped out somewhere and was lost.
payload.problem: Aditya lost the letter on the way

payload.title: Where Is the Notebook
payload.text: Veer needed his maths notebook very badly for the very next class, where the teacher would surely check all the homework. He opened his school bag and tipped everything out onto the desk to find it quickly. He looked again and again, shaking out every single book and folder, growing more worried by the minute. His friends even helped him hunt through the pile of things. But it was no use at all, because the maths notebook was just not there anywhere in the whole class.

payload.title: Bag in the Auto
payload.text: Meera came back home from school in a noisy auto-rickshaw one tiring afternoon. The ride was bumpy and she was very sleepy, so when the auto reached her gate she jumped down quickly to hurry inside the house. The auto driver drove away down the road before she had even reached the front door. She did not notice anything wrong at first. Only much later, when she looked for her things, did she realise with a gasp that she had left her whole school bag behind on the back seat.

payload.title: The Missing Key
payload.text: Sara walked home from school and reached her front door, all ready to go straight inside for a snack. She put her hand into her pocket to take out the house key that her mother had carefully given her that morning. To her surprise, the pocket was completely empty. She turned out both pockets and searched her bag, but the key was simply not there. She had carried it all day long, but somewhere at school it must have slipped out and got lost.

payload.title: Giving It Back
payload.text: Arjun found a beautiful blue pen lying forgotten on the classroom floor, right near the door. It was exactly the kind of smooth, shiny pen he had always wished he owned, and no one in the room was watching him at all. For just a second, he thought of quietly slipping it into his own bag and keeping it. But then he imagined how sad and upset the owner must be feeling. So he asked around the whole class and returned the pen to the right boy with a smile.
payload.problem: Arjun returned the lost pen to its owner
problemDecoys: Arjun had lost his own pen

payload.text: The friendly cricket match on the field had just come to an end, and all the boys were busy packing up to head home. When her mother finally called her to come home, she ran off in a hurry and forgot her water bottle sitting on the bench.

payload.title: No Ruler in Sight
payload.text: Ishaan had to draw a perfectly straight line for the neat diagram in his science book. He reached confidently into his pencil box for his ruler, the very same one he always kept inside it. To his great surprise, the box held only a stub of pencil and a tiny eraser. The ruler had gone missing somewhere, and he could not find it anywhere in the class.

payload.title: Lost a Shoe
payload.text: It was the games period, and Riya was running as fast as her legs could carry her across the wide school field. Right in the middle of her speedy sprint, one of her shoes came loose and flew right off her foot into the air. She was so caught up in the race that she did not even notice it had gone and kept on running. Only when the game ended did she look down at her bare foot in shock. She went back to search, but the shoe was lost somewhere in the long grass.
payload.problem: Riya lost one of her shoes

payload.title: Teddy at the Mall
payload.text: Ananya went shopping with her mother at the big, bright mall and carried her favourite teddy bear everywhere with her. While she was busy looking at a shiny new toy on display, she placed her teddy down on a low shelf for just a moment. Then she and her mother moved on to other shops, rode up the escalator, and bought many things. Ananya was so excited that she completely forgot about her teddy. When they finally reached home, she looked for her teddy and realised, with tears in her eyes, that it was gone.

payload.title: Toy by the Gate
payload.text: Karan was happily spinning his small wooden toy top near the society gate one quiet afternoon. A friendly little street dog wandered past him, wagging its tail, so Karan put his toy down on the ground to gently pet the dog. The dog was so playful and fun that Karan forgot all about his beloved top for a long while. He laughed and chased the dog around the gate. When he finally turned back to pick up his toy, he found that it had rolled away somewhere and was completely lost.

payload.title: Money at the Market
payload.text: Vikram's mother sent him to the busy, crowded market to buy some sweet apples for the evening. She handed him a crisp ten-rupee note, and he held it tightly in his fist all the way there. As he reached out his hand to pick up the reddest, juiciest apple from the pile, the note slipped from his fingers without him noticing. In the noisy, pushing crowd of shoppers, it fluttered away and was instantly gone. He searched the ground at his feet, but his money was lost.

payload.title: Returning the Book
payload.text: Anjali spotted a colourful storybook lying forgotten under a bench in the quiet corner of her classroom. There was no name written anywhere on the cover, and she could easily have kept the lovely book all for herself without anyone knowing. But as she held it, she remembered how much she loved her own books and how very sad she would feel if she ever lost one of them. She knew exactly what the right thing to do was. So she asked around carefully, found the owner, and gave the book back with a kind smile.
payload.problem: Anjali returned the lost book to its owner
problemDecoys: Anjali had lost her own book

payload.title: Missing Paintbrush
payload.text: During the art class, Sneha was very excited to paint a bright blue sky filled with soft, fluffy white clouds. She reached into her box to take out her trusty paintbrush, but to her surprise it was not there at all. She looked all around the table, peered under her chair, and even gently asked her neighbour if they had seen it. Everyone shook their heads and shrugged. No matter where she searched, the paintbrush was simply nowhere to be found, and her painting could not begin.

payload.title: The Doll Fell
payload.text: Ravi was happily playing with his most favourite doll in the living room at home one afternoon. He tossed it high up into the air, again and again, trying to catch it neatly each time, as if it were a fun game. He grew bolder and threw it higher with every toss, laughing all the while. payload.title: Pencil Snapped
payload.text: Priya was writing her homework in class and wanted all her letters to look very dark, bold, and neat on the page. She pressed the pencil down harder and harder against the paper, trying to make the writing stand out clearly. She did not realise just how much pressure she was putting on the thin wooden pencil. The pencil bent slightly under her hand. Then, with a sudden sharp crack that everyone nearby could hear, the pencil snapped cleanly into two separate pieces.

payload.title: A Torn Page
payload.text: Aarav was reading a very thrilling adventure story at home one quiet evening, all curled up on the sofa. He reached a most exciting part of the tale and simply could not wait to find out what happened next to the brave hero. In his great hurry and excitement, he grabbed the corner of the page and turned it far too quickly and carelessly. The thin paper caught on his finger and ripped with a loud tearing sound. One whole page of his lovely book was now badly torn.

payload.title: The Dented Wheel
payload.text: Anaya loved riding her shiny new cycle round and round the society every single evening after she finished her homework. One day she was happily racing her best friend and pedalled very fast as she neared the society gate. She was looking back at her friend and laughing, so she did not notice a big grey stone lying right in her path. She rode straight over it with a hard bump. The front wheel bent badly out of shape, and after that the cycle could no longer roll straight.

payload.title: Wheel Popped Off
payload.text: Kabir was racing his little red toy car across the smooth, shiny floor of his home one rainy afternoon. He wanted to find out just how fast the small car could really go, so he pushed it harder and harder with each turn. The car zoomed faster and faster across the wide room, almost too quick to see. Then it crashed straight into the bottom of the wall with a loud bang. One of its four little wheels popped right off and rolled away under the sofa.

payload.title: A Cracked Piece
payload.text: Diya was busy building a big, colourful jigsaw puzzle on the floor of her room at home. She had worked on it for a long time and had almost finished the lovely picture when she suddenly felt very thirsty. She got up quickly to fetch a glass of cool water from the kitchen. In her hurry, she completely forgot that one little puzzle piece was still lying on the floor right behind her. When she walked back, she stepped on it without looking, and it cracked.

payload.title: Kite Caught a Wire
payload.text: Aditya was flying his bright orange kite from the terrace on a lovely, windy afternoon. The strong, steady breeze lifted his kite higher and higher into the clear blue sky, and he felt very proud as it danced above the rooftops. He let out more and more string, wanting it to fly the highest of all. But then a sudden strong gust pulled the kite sharply sideways towards the electric wires. The kite got tangled around a wire, tugged hard, and tore right down the middle.

payload.title: Crack in the Bat
payload.text: Veer was batting in a fun, friendly cricket match on the field with all his neighbourhood friends. The bowler, who was the fastest in the group, ran in and hurled the hard ball towards him at full speed. Veer planted his feet, lifted his bat high, and swung at the ball with every bit of strength he had, hoping to hit a huge six. The ball struck the very edge of the bat with a loud thwack. A long, jagged crack appeared right along the side of his cricket bat.

payload.title: The String Snapped
payload.text: Meera was proudly showing off her very best yoyo tricks to her cousin in the living room at home. She spun the bright yoyo round and round, faster and faster, working up to a very tricky loop high in the air. Her cousin clapped and cheered, so she spun it even harder to impress him more. The yoyo string was old and worn thin, but she did not notice this at all. With a sudden, sharp ping, the string snapped, and the yoyo flew right across the room.

payload.title: Crack in the Drum
payload.text: Sara had just received a brand-new toy drum and was very excited to play it loudly at home. She banged on it happily, making louder and louder beats to call everyone in the house to come and listen to her music. She hit the drum harder each time, wanting to make the very biggest, boomiest sound of all. Her hands flew up and down with great energy. After one especially strong and heavy hit, a thin crack appeared right across the top skin of the drum.

payload.title: Fixing It With Mom
payload.text: Arjun's favourite toy plane slipped off the high shelf at home and came crashing down hard onto the floor. One of its wings snapped right off, and Arjun felt so terribly sad that his eyes quickly filled up with tears. He was sure that his beloved plane was now ruined forever and could never fly again. He sat down on the floor, holding the broken pieces. Then his kind mother came and sat beside him, found some strong glue in the drawer, and together they carefully fixed the broken plane.

payload.title: The Robot Stopped
payload.text: Rohan absolutely loved his toy robot, which could walk on its own, blink its bright eyes, and make funny beeping sounds. He played with it every single day after school in his room at home, treating it like a real little friend. One afternoon, while making the robot dance on the edge of the table, he was not watching closely enough. The robot stepped right off the edge and landed hard on the floor below. After that big fall, it stopped moving altogether and went completely silent.

payload.title: A Leg Came Off
payload.text: Tara was galloping her smooth wooden toy horse across the floor at home, pretending the whole time that it was running in a grand and important race. To make the race even more exciting and dramatic, she decided to make the toy horse leap high over a thick book lying on the ground. She lifted it up and brought it down fast on the other side. The horse landed badly with a loud thud against the floor. One of its four little wooden legs snapped clean off.

payload.title: Guitar String Broke
payload.text: Ishaan had a small toy guitar that he absolutely loved to strum while pretending to be a famous rock star at home. He wanted to play a really loud and powerful tune for his whole family that evening after dinner. So he pulled and plucked the strings as hard as he possibly could, over and over again, to make a big sound. He did not notice that one string was stretching far too tightly. Suddenly the thin string stretched past its limit and broke with a loud, sharp twang.

payload.title: Brother Broke It
payload.text: Riya had kept her brand-new favourite toy very carefully on the table at home before going off to wash her hands for dinner. While she was busy in the bathroom, her curious little brother spotted the shiny new toy and reached up to pick it up so he could play with it too. His small hands were not big enough to hold it properly, and it began to slip. He tried to catch it but failed. The toy fell straight down onto the floor and broke into many small pieces.
payload.problem: Riya's toy got broken by her brother

payload.title: Duck Split Open
payload.text: Ananya always played with her cheerful yellow rubber duck during bath time at home every night. She especially loved how the little duck made a funny, high squeak whenever she pressed it down underwater. So she began to squeeze it harder and harder each day, trying to make the loudest and funniest squeak of all. The rubber slowly grew weak from all that squeezing. After many, many tight squeezes, the duck finally split right open along its side and never squeaked again.

payload.title: Toy Snapped in Half
payload.text: Karan was very curious about how his shiny new plastic toy worked on the inside. He turned it over and over in his hands, looking carefully for any way to open it up and peek into its hidden parts. Slowly, he began to bend it this way and that way, pressing a little harder each time, just to see if it would come apart neatly. The plastic groaned under his fingers. It could not take so much bending and pressing for long, and finally it snapped right in half with a loud crack.

payload.title: Train Lost a Coach
payload.text: Vikram was pulling his long toy train across the floor of his room at home one rainy day. The train had a shiny engine and many little coaches joined together one after another with tiny metal hooks. He wanted the train to go really, really fast around the room, so he yanked the string hard with a sudden, sharp jerk. The jerk was far too strong for the little hooks to hold. With a snap, one of the small coaches broke away and was left behind on the floor.

payload.title: Fix, Don't Throw
payload.text: Anjali's soft toy bunny tore at the seam while she was playing with it on her bed at home. Some of the soft white stuffing began to poke out through the hole, and her mother gently said that it might be best to simply throw the old bunny away. But Anjali had loved that little bunny ever since she was a tiny baby, and she did not want to lose it at all. She thought hard for a moment about what to do. Then she chose to mend it carefully with a needle and thread instead of throwing it out.

payload.title: The Cracked Flute
payload.text: Sneha had left her favourite toy flute lying on the chair after happily playing a tune with it at home. A little while later, she came hurrying back into the room, talking to her brother and not looking carefully at where she was about to sit down. She plopped down onto the chair without a second thought and sat right on top of the flute. There was a sudden loud crunch from beneath her. When she jumped up and looked, a long crack ran all the way across her toy flute.

payload.title: Sharing the Mango
payload.text: There was only one ripe, juicy yellow mango left in the fruit bowl at home that warm afternoon. Both Ravi and his younger sister spotted the lovely mango at exactly the same moment, and both of them wanted to eat it very badly. Ravi knew that he was bigger and stronger, so he could simply grab the mango and keep the whole thing for himself if he wished. He looked at his sister's hopeful face. Instead of being greedy, he cut the mango neatly in two and gave his sister an equal half.
payload.problem: Ravi wanted to share the last mango fairly

payload.title: Taking Turns
